What do you think about when rent is due?
When the bank takes your pay every Friday,
And bills keep coming in each day and date,
Do you worry that they will say no more?

My friend, your heart will break,
And that's okay.
To be human is to feel.
I can't stop the tears from falling. Stop what? What I've been doing all my life?
Not getting caught up in a goodnight kiss, but taking it home with me and then waking up remembering every detail when you wake next day and look at me as though this has changed something because how can these feelings not effect both of us if we go back now?
It was our mistake for never stopping. Now there is nothing between us or beside us anymore, just space where people have stood before their bodies are found again.
We shouldn’t touch them anyway. They’re dead.
That must hurt so much. And it’s impossible to make everything work out like they did on TV shows. That takes an hour too long in real life.
There should probably be another poem about the man who tried to bury his son away from home, which he wasn’t sure was wrong, until someone asked him why he left so many doors unlocked? But by then it was too late; the first time had come around already while waiting here.

Text:
Brother, I'll take care of you. When the world takes from your heart,
I will be there to hear it out; Give me a chance and I’ll give my best.
If they have cut down all that grows inside you - if their lies made you believe them,
Give me another breath as I ease this pain away.
Brother, we can start anew. And begin again with no trace;
The wounds inflicted on you by those who thought less than human,
Are only marks for us together now so strong when our time has come

Monday, September 7th – Wednesday the next morning.
“Mom!” I call her name out in a voice that is both surprised and irritated. And it really isn't polite to shout at someone who is standing on your property because she apparently thinks you have something of hers. But there are times when manners come second, especially if they involve your family’s history being dragged up by an ex-wife you haven’t seen since high school.
My mother takes no notice from where she stands in my hallway. She stares over me with cold eyes until we lock eyes directly across each other; then she raises an eyebrow as though asking why did I say anything about this? A shrug of mine says nothing.
“So what are you doing here?” I ask once again. This time the question comes out much more even than before which means whatever conversation we share today won't go into too great details regarding our last meeting back when all this was just beginning for us. My parents eventually split ways after having five children altogether (four boys including myself), but my sister ended things abruptly without giving anyone any sort of explanation beyond dropping off divorce papers one day during breakfast while everyone else tried their best not look shocked or confused.
It wasn't long afterwards when tensions between them increased greatly resulting in fights every now-and-then which were usually followed by loud arguments late nights filled mostly silence save few words exchanged sometimes through clenched teeth. Back then nobody thought twice seeing how normal divorces can be except maybe some extra emotional stress put upon those living within same household given circumstances surrounding event itself such as separation agreement reached beforehand along lines describing shared responsibilities amongst former spouses post-breakup etcetera ad infinitum...
But anyways getting back onto point right away - yeah so obviously enough said above applies completely unlike situation presented currently wherein case instead finding ourselves face-to-face unexpectedly mid-morning yesterday afternoon following sudden visitation request issued via email addressed

**Last Bus Home**
1. My father's face illuminated by moonlight
as he waves goodbye through shattered glass.
He's forgotten our address in his mind's eye,
yet knows exactly where to look at nightfall.
2. The girl with silver hair curls her lips up high
like she expects angels flying down low skies;
she finds comfort hiding there among strangers –-
her only sanctuary when everything goes wrong again.

wringing hands like suds while tears run streams away;

An ankle monitor is a device used to track an individual's location and movements. The term refers specifically to electronic monitoring devices, such as GPS trackers or radio frequency monitors.
So what does that have to do with me?
I was first introduced to the idea of ankle monitoring in my second year at University when I took Criminal Law. We were talking about different forms of penal sanctions. What are these? How do they work? Why would we use them instead of prison sentences? And so on...
What really struck me though, after hearing all this chatter from our lecturer, who clearly had no love for the system he worked within (he always gave us great ideas for exam questions too), was not so much the concepts behind each form of punishment but rather how people described their purpose(s). For example:
* Restorative Justice – Focuses primarily upon repairing harms caused by offending behaviour; helping both victims & offenders alike.
* Deterrence - Designed mainly around discouraging future crimes through fear factor associated w/ potential consequences experienced following initial offence committment

Lorenzo de Medici died April 9, in a palace garden where he loved to stroll. The people of Florence mourned him so that when his brother Piero the Younger ascended the throne their sorrow for Lorenzo turned into hatred.
The first thing they did was destroy every statue and painting depicting Lorenzo as he had been both anointed by God with the new name Augustus on account of being Florence’s patron prince but also because of what he represented—the harmony of Florentine art at its zenith.
But not all agreed such destruction should be permitted. There were those who maintained it would have done more good if instead of destroying these works the paintings and statues representing “Florence's beloved” (as Francesco Salviati called them) could have preserved their memory alive through imitation while providing guidance to future generations which is always much preferable than total obliteration.
This view received support from another party within power structure itself namely cardinal Silvio Passerini; however there existed opposing factions among members leading up to this decision including some high officials closely connected with Pico della Mirandola himself whose request led eventually towards implementation thereof despite opposition faced along way during process due primarily political considerations rather than religious sentiments alone since everyone knew better than go against wishes great saintly man whom recent history recorded having given away almost everything personal possession out handiest ever possible

Today we look at Ephesians 4:29-32:
Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up, as fits the occasion, that it may give grace to those who hear. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and slander be put away from you, along with all malice. Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you.
Corrupting thoughts cannot stay inside our heart; they must flow through us if left unchecked! This applies whether you’re on social media or talking face-to-face about any situation in this life!
What could build them up within their own souls? Is there something we can take away as well?
Answer my question please!
In times of conflict, remember Paul's words above - keep focus on kindness instead of trying to bring others down (Acts 17:6). Practice forgiveness daily until everyone around understands love conquers hate every single time.

In the house of grandma where all things are kept and shown, is a table with chairs that she gives us to join her there. The old wooden tables we sit at every day.
The walls in this room hang pictures from days gone by showing people who were dear to momma before they passed away. There was also a piano for when you wanted to sing along as well to your own song.
On nights spent together around fires made up for our story time, each chair held those close or far apart until it came down again like sand on its way home.
No person shall be left out because then grandma would feel alone; so come take one now please and remember not just your place but mine too within these places called ours forevermore.
